intended_object: For a word w ∈ {true,false}ⁿ and morphisms α : U' → U, β : V' → V in a monoidal category, the morphism (…((𝟙 ⊗ γ₁) ⊗ γ₂) ⊗ … ⊗ γₙ) : wordPow U' V' n w → wordPow U V n w, where γᵢ = α if wᵢ = true and β otherwise. This is the action on morphisms of the word-power functor (X,Y) ↦ X^{w}. I took this from the docstring and from how the module uses it (`wordMap_natural`).
explanation:
`wordPow X Y n w` is built by recursion: the unit for n = 0, and otherwise `wordPow X Y n (w ∘ castSucc) ⊗ (bif w (last n) then X else Y)`. `wordCongrMap` follows exactly the same recursion on morphisms: `𝟙 (𝟙_ A)` for n = 0, and for n + 1 the tensor `⊗ₘ` of the recursive map with `letterCongr α β (w (last n))`, which is α on a `true` letter and β on a `false` one. So it is the letterwise tensor of α and β along the word, with the same source and target as the word powers. That is what the docstring says, and it is the morphism part of the word-power functor. Its main use is `wordMap_natural`, which says that it is natural against `wordMap`; that statement checks out by `tensorHom_comp_tensorHom`.

The definition works in any monoidal category, with no braiding or symmetry needed, which is the natural setting. Mathlib has no notion of word powers or of a letterwise tensor of two morphisms along a Boolean word, so there is no more general counterpart that it duplicates. The degenerate case n = 0 gives the identity on the unit object, which is correct.
